chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Utaibah, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If you pray while walking, you say the Takbir, then walk and recite; when you intend to bow, you gesture with the bow, then you gesture with the prostration; and there is no voluntary prayer during travel."
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer and handle voluntary prayers while walking during travel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the practical mechanics of *salat al-khafif* (lightened prayer) during travel, specifying that recitation occurs while walking with gestures indicating bowing and prostration rather than full physical postures. It further clarifies the jurisprudential consensus that voluntary (*nafl*) prayers are suspended during travel to prioritize the obligatory duties, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease (*rukhsah*) in times of hardship. This ruling is foundational in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for distinguishing between the full prayer of residence and the abbreviated prayer of journey.
